transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Partnerships), Jordan Reyes (Stratus), Priya Nair (Stratus), Dan Vogel (Stratus)

Summary: quick partner intro, high-level capabilities, fit for GPU hosting + systems integration. Covered hosted vs dedicated, private/VPC options, KMS/e2e encryption, SOC2 compliance, pilot ideas and benchmarking.

Topics: partner model, integration touchpoints, benchmarking, pricing, security/compliance, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm joined by Maya our SE and Samir from partnerships. Uh, Jordan, Priya, Dan, great to see you, thanks for making time.
[00:32] Jordan (Stratus): Yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it. Quick intros from our side 

- I'm Jordan, head of partnerships at Stratus, Priya does cloud integrations and Dan is our GPU architecture lead. We're excited to learn about Redwood and see where we align.
[01:05] Alex: Great. Real quick agenda, we wanted to intro Redwood's partner program, surface where integrations typically live (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and hear Stratus's priorities for cloud and GPU stack so we can map opportunities. Sound good?
[01:37] Priya (Stratus): Sounds good, we basically want to evaluate whether this is a tech partnership (we resell / co-deploy) or more of a referral/integration. Also interested in performance numbers 

- latency, throughput, and quantized model support.
[02:10] Maya (Redwood SE): Totally. High level 

- Redwood runs three deployment modes: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools, and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem installs. Our runtime has KV cache, batching, and selection logic to pick kernels based on model and hardware.
[02:45] Dan (Stratus): When you say KV cache and batching, is that application-visible or totally managed? We have customers who want per-session cache control 

- some want sticky session affinity.
[03:12] Maya: It's managed but configurable. You can control prefix caching TTLs and routing policies, including session affinity if you need. There's an API flag and in Dedicated you can set policies at pool level.
[03:38] Jordan: Nice. On the partnership side, our main ask: how easy is automation for provisioning Dedicated pools on Stratus infra? We want to automate capacity provisioning and billing reconciliation.
[04:10] Samir (Redwood Partnerships): We do programmatic provisioning APIs for Dedicated capacity, and we expose usage metrics for billing. For partners we can provide a reseller flow or delegated admin APIs. We typically integrate with partner billing via metered usage exports (CSV/BigQuery).
[04:45] Priya: Ok, what about private deployments 

- VPC or air-gapped? Customers in banking/regulatory space ask for HSM/KMS and audit logs.
[05:10] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking and optional on-prem package. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management, and we ship audit logs and syslogs to customer endpoints. SOC 2 is standard for hosted; additional compliance add-ons available.
[05:45] Dan: Any gotchas around GPUs 

- like driver versions, MIG support, multi-instance GPU splitting?
[06:10] Maya: We support common NVIDIA stacks and have tested with MIG in certain configurations; we can provide recommended AMIs and container images. For multi-instance, there are perf tradeoffs; we can share quantized kernel profiles and guidance.
[06:42] Jordan: From a commercial POV, what's the typical model? Resell margins, co-sell credit?
[07:05] Samir: We have a partner program with referral and reseller tiers. Margins depend on commitment levels; for Dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts. For SI partners we offer implementation credits and joint go-to-market resources. We'll send the partner program doc.
[07:40] Priya: Great. On performance, can you share any numbers for 7B/13B/70B models on, say, A100 and H100?
[08:05] Maya: Ballpark, for a well-optimized 13B on A100 we see p99 latency in the 40-80ms per-token range under batching scenarios, 70B more like 120-250ms depending on quantization and kernel selection. On H100 those numbers drop but also depend on batch size and sequence length. We'll send a small benchmark matrix; note these are indicative.
[08:40] Dan: Do you support int8/int4 quantization in the runtime? We have customers who want to trade quality for throughput.
[09:05] Maya: Yes, we have quantization-friendly execution paths and will recommend quant profiles per workload. We also support model variants so you can fallback to FP16 for higher quality.
[09:40] Jordan: Any native integrations with provisioning or orchestration tools we already use? We use Terraform/Crossplane and an internal control-plane.
[10:05] Alex: We expose Terraform providers for some aspects and a REST API for the rest. For partners we can provide a Terraform module and example crossplane provider config.
[10:35] Priya: Good. Compliance questions: do you have SOC2 Type II and do you provide audit-ready logs and SSO?
[10:55] Maya: Yes SOC 2 Type II for hosted, SSO via SAML/SSO/OIDC, RBAC at token and org levels, and logs are streamable. For Private we hand over the control plane and can integrate with customer's SSO and KMS.
[11:30] Dan: How about data residency? We need to pin data to certain regions for some customers.
[11:50] Alex: We have region-aware routing and can pin workloads to specific regions. In Dedicated/Private you can choose region and even exclusive pools.
[12:15] Jordan: On integration ops, what's the typical effort for a Dedicated integration with a partner cloud? Weeks? Months?
[12:40] Maya: For a straightforward Dedicated resell it's usually 4-6 weeks for provisioning, integration with billing and monitoring; for full Private deployments with custom networking it's more like 8-12 weeks depending on approvals.
[13:05] Priya: Are there any customers doing SIs resell where Redwood runs the control plane and partner provides infra?
[13:25] Samir: Yes, we have a hybrid where Redwood control plane manages model versions and routing while partner provides the GPU infra; that tends to be our fastest path to market.
[13:50] Jordan: That could be interesting. We want a model where Stratus sells GPU capacity and we bundle Redwood as managed inference.
[14:12] Dan: On metrics and logging, can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces?
[14:38] Maya: Yep that's in Redwood Console - token-level cost, per-route dashboards, traces and error analysis. We can expose those via APIs for partner dashboards.
[15:05] Jordan: Okay let's talk pilot ideas. We could spin up a small Dedicated pool on Stratus hardware and run a 2-week benchmark with a sample workload. What would you want from us?
[15:30] Maya: We'll want target models, expected QPS, seq length distribution, desired latency SLOs, and whether to test quantized variants. If you can provide instance types and estimated GPU counts that's helpful.
[15:58] Jordan: We can provide a proposed inventory (regions and instance types). We'll also need a simple SLA/contract for the pilot.
[16:20] Samir: We'll draft a pilot statement of work and a quick partner MOU.
[16:40] Priya: On billing reconciliation - do you provide daily metered usage?
[16:58] Alex: We expose usage exports and daily summaries, and for partners we can provide metered CSVs or BigQuery exports for automated reconciliation.
[17:18] Dan: A few technical clarifications - is there support for multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated? We want strong tenant isolation for customers.
[17:40] Maya: Dedicated pools are logically isolated and you can opt for tenant-level RBAC and network segmentation. For stricter guarantees we'd recommend Private deployments.
[18:05] Jordan: Competitive landscape - we're seeing interest in Lambda and CoreWeave. How do you differentiate?
[18:30] Alex: Our differentiation is production-first tooling: per-token cost visibility, KV caching, smart routing, and unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private. We also put a lot into developer DX and rollout controls.
[18:55] Priya: Any partner references you can share?
[19:12] Samir: We have a few telecom and fintech partners on dedicated and private, we'll share anonymized case studies.
[19:35] Dan: For the benchmark, do you have a standard harness? We use a variety of models.
[19:55] Maya: We have a benchmark checklist and harness; I'll send that. It includes payload shapes, seq lengths, warmup runs and SLO targets.
[20:20] Jordan: Ok, on the legal/commercial -- IP concerns: if we co-deploy, who owns the customer relationship and outputs?
[20:42] Alex: That's flexible. For resell partnerships typically partner holds customer contract and Redwood provides the software and support per partner MSA. For co-managed models we can negotiate shared support responsibilities. We'll have legal draft options.
[21:05] Priya: Any limitations around VPC peering?
[21:22] Maya: We support VPC peering and private link-like setups; for air-gapped customers we do an on-prem package.
[21:40] Jordan: How about automatic fallback policies - if Stratus pool is overloaded can requests fall back to Redwood hosted?
[21:58] Maya: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks (region, cost, latency). We can configure auto-fallback to hosted or to another model variant.
[22:20] Dan: For GPU vendors, what driver stacks are recommended? We run a mix of A100 and H100 with nvidia driver 535-ish.
[22:40] Maya: We publish recommended stacks; 535 or newer for H100 is fine, we'll verify compatibility.
[23:05] Jordan: Great. On the partner go-to-market, do you have co-marketing funds or joint webinars?
[23:25] Samir: Yes, depending on the partnership level we offer co-marketing funds, joint case studies, and PR support.
[23:45] Priya: Any onboarding cost? Some partners require onboarding credits to cover SE time.
[24:03] Alex: For initial pilots we usually offer implementation credits; for larger engagements we bill SE time or roll into reseller margins.
[24:25] Jordan: Ok, let's flip to potential risks - from our side customers worry about vendor lock-in and model portability. How do you address that?
[24:45] Maya: We support standard model formats and version pinning; customers can bring their own models and we support exportable configs. We also provide migration guides.
[25:05] Dan: Latency benchmarks matter a lot; we'd want to run a POC with representative customer traffic, not just synthetic loads.
[25:25] Maya: Agreed - we'll work with you to set up a realistic load profile for the pilot.
[25:45] Alex: Quick note on pricing: hosted is usage-based per token/token type, Dedicated is reserved capacity commitments (monthly/annual), and for Private it's licensing plus support. We'll share a pricing sheet.
[26:10] Jordan: Good. Do you have any specific partner integration prerequisites? (APIs, certs, security review)
[26:30] Samir: Standard: SOC2 report, SAML metadata for SSO, API keys provisioning, and a technical contact. We can hand you a checklist.
[26:55] Priya: For pilots where we run infra, how do you handle upgrades and kernel changes?
[27:15] Maya: Upgrades are coordinated; we do canary deploys and can run them in maintenance windows. For Dedicated we can schedule kernel/driver update windows with you.
[27:40] Dan: Any specific monitoring integrations for Prometheus/Grafana?
[27:58] Maya: Yes we can export metrics to Prometheus and dashboards to Grafana; for partners we can share read-only dashboards.
[28:20] Jordan: On the technical deep-dive - we'd like to cover kernel selection and quantization behavior. Can Maya lead that?
[28:40] Maya: Absolutely, I'd be happy to. Maybe schedule a 60-90 minute SE deep-dive with sample models and logs.
[29:00] Alex: Action items recap - we'll send partner program doc, pricing, benchmark checklist. Maya will share the harness and lead the SE deep-dive. Jordan will send region/capacity targets.
[29:30] Priya: Timeline-wise, we can aim for pilot kick-off mid-April; realistic?
[29:48] Samir: That aligns with our internal timelines too. If Jordan can share capacity by 2025-04-15 we can prepare infra.
[30:10] Jordan: We'll try to accelerate and get that to you. One more thing, do you have a partner portal or sandbox account?
[30:30] Alex: We have a partner sandbox org and a portal with docs, partner APIs, and example Terraform modules. We'll provision an account for Stratus.
[31:00] Dan: Great. Any blockers you foresee from your side for a co-deploy?
[31:18] Maya: Mostly network approvals and legal; technically it's straightforward.
[31:35] Jordan: Ok sounds good. A couple of small clarifications in chat: (1) pilot size suggestions; (2) we have a customer who needs FIPS 140-2 KMS, is that supported?
[31:58] Maya: FIPS support is available via partner KMS integrations; we'll confirm specifics in follow-up.
[32:20] Alex: We'll include that in the security/controls doc.
[32:40] Jordan: Anything else for the pilot?
[32:55] Maya: If you can provide a representative prompt set and target SLOs, that speeds things up.
[33:15] Priya: We'll compile a short sample set and share.
[33:35] Jordan: Regarding upsell, would Redwood offer co-sell credit if we drive enterprise deals?
[33:55] Samir: Yes for qualified deals we offer co-sell support and margin; exact terms in partner MSA.
[34:15] Dan: Tech question - do you provide model caching at edge or only in-region?
[34:37] Maya: Currently in-region caching; we do have edge options for certain partners but would need to scope.
[34:55] Jordan: Okay. Anything about long-term roadmap that's relevant?
[35:12] Alex: We're investing in routing policies, smarter KV cache, and expanded telemetry for partners; also more infra partner automations.
[35:35] Priya: Sounds aligned.
[35:50] Jordan: Let's recap next steps.
[36:05] Alex: Recap: 1) Alex send partner deck + pricing by 2025-04-11. 2) Maya share benchmark harness and schedule SE deep-dive week of 2025-04-21. 3) Jordan provide region/capacity targets by 2025-04-15. 4) Samir draft pilot SOW and partner MOU.
[36:35] Priya: I'll follow up with our legal lead about MSA templates.
[36:50] Jordan: We'll also try to map a customer to include in the pilot.
[37:10] Maya: One small note on data: for pilot logs we can route to your logging endpoint - we'll send instructions.
[37:30] Dan: Cool. Any final questions?
[37:45] Alex: Not from us, appreciate the time. We'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[38:05] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Quick note, deffer - there's some background noise sorry if the transcript lopped some words.
[38:25] Samir: No problem.
[38:40] Alex: Ok we'll close - thanks and talk soon.
[38:50] End of recording
